requirement: The vehicle control system must include electronic signal filtering to mitigate the effects of electromagnetic interference (EMI) on sensor signals
The ECU must perform self-diagnostics to ensure its health and operational integrity at startup and during operation
Secure communication protocols must be implemented to prevent unauthorized access or tampering with drive-by-wire signals
The system must monitor its power supply and have a backup to maintain functionality in the event of a power interruption
The sensor must maintain calibration over time and under variable environmental conditions without the need for frequent re-calibration
In case of sensor failure, the system must revert to a fail-safe mode that allows for controlled and safe vehicle operation
The steering system  must transfer the driver's input with minimal torsional deflection to ensure accurate steering input
The steering system must provide consistent feedback to the driver under various driving conditions
In case of power steering failure, the system should allow for manual steering control with an acceptable increase in effort
The steering system must include mechanisms to damp excessive vibrations from being transmitted to the steering wheel
Power steering systems must provide the correct level of assist to the driver, adjusting based on vehicle speed and steering angle
EPS systems must include fault detection mechanisms that alert the driver to malfunctions and, where possible, provide a fail-operational mode
Systems must monitor for hydraulic fluid contamination and deterioration, providing maintenance alerts as needed
In the event of power steering failure, the vehicle must still be steerable by manual means, although increased effort may be required
Torque sensors in EPS systems must be calibrated to accurately measure driver input, ensuring appropriate steering assist
Power steering systems, whether hydraulic or electronic, must operate effectively in a wide range of environmental conditions, including extreme temperatures
The steering system must provide tactile feedback to the driver that is proportional to the driving conditions and steering input
Steering systems must be capable of handling the expected range of loads without failure or excessive play developing over time
In the absence of power assist, the manual steering effort required should comply with safety standards to ensure that the vehicle can still be controlled
The vehicle must provide appropriate feedback to the driver through the steering mechanism, allowing for intuitive assessment of road conditions and vehicle behavior
Power steering assistance should be consistent across different steering angles and not impair the driver's ability to perform smooth cornering maneuvers
The steering system must provide consistent feedback to the driver, regardless of interventions from safety and assistance systems
The steering system should adapt sensitivity based on vehicle speed, with lower sensitivity at higher speeds for improved steering stability
The steering system must provide adequate feedback to the driver to convey the status of the steering control, especially in the event of a system degradation
The system shall retain fault information in memory to aid in diagnostics and troubleshooting even after the vehicle is turned off
The vehicle's control system must adjust braking and acceleration to optimize tire grip during winter driving conditions
In the event of understeer, the system must adjust power distribution and braking to aid in returning to the intended path
Stability control systems must be responsive during cornering to counteract any excessive torsional force that may upset vehicle balance
Traction control systems must adapt to varying road surfaces to maintain tire grip and vehicle control
The vehicle's onboard systems must continuously analyze dynamic behavior and adjust stability and traction controls accordingly
The steering system must adjust the torque assist based on the vehicle's speed to ensure appropriate steering feedback and control
The system must monitor tire grip levels and adjust steering torque to compensate for changes in grip
The steering system must adapt the torque levels in response to detected road surface conditions (e.g., ice, water, gravel)
The steering system must perform consistently across a range of environmental conditions, including temperature extremes and humidity
The steering system should adapt the steering feel according to the driving mode selected (e.g., comfort vs. sporty)
The system must adjust steering sensitivity in real-time based on vehicle speed, steering angle, and driver input
The steering system must have a redundant mechanism to maintain steering control in the event of a single point of failure
The steering system must maintain optimal feedback and performance under various environmental conditions, including temperature and humidity extremes
The steering system should be capable of providing haptic feedback to alert the driver of potential hazards or system states
The response of the steering system to sensor input must not exceed a specified time limit to ensure timely intervention by ESC and Lane Keeping Assist systems
In case of steering system electronic failures, the system must ensure the retention of emergency manual steering control
The vehicle's onboard diagnostic system must alert the driver or technician to any wear or imminent failure of steering components
The system should record steering performance data to aid in troubleshooting and predictive maintenance
In case of partial system failure, the steering assist must either maintain operation at a reduced level or fail-safe
The system must adapt the steering force required in response to vehicle speed and driving conditions
The steering system must include comprehensive diagnostic capabilities to detect and signal any malfunction
The system must enable a manual override allowing the driver to steer without assist in case of system failure
Steering assistance must vary proportionally to the vehicle's cornering speed as influenced by the accelerator pedal position to provide optimal driver feedback and contro
The system must compensate for crosswinds by adjusting steering angle and acceleration inputs to maintain the intended cornering path
The control system must detect and mitigate power oversteer by adjusting the steering angle and acceleration pedal inputs to maintain vehicle control
The vehicle control system must provide feedback for brake modulation through the acceleration pedal to assist with precise steering inputs
The vehicle control systems must include adaptive modes that adjust the sensitivity of the steering and acceleration in response to the assessed skill level of the driver
Upon throttle lift-off during a lane change, the vehicle control system must adapt steering assistance to maintain a safe trajectory
The system should impose steering angle limitations when aggressive acceleration is detected to prevent loss of control during lane changes
The control system must have the capability to perform real-time adjustments to both steering and throttle during lane change maneuvers to maintain balance and vehicle poise
The steering system must adjust feedback and responsiveness based on real-time traffic conditions data, enhancing control during lane changes in congested areas
The lane-keeping assist system must take into account lane congestion to provide appropriate steering assistance, reducing driver fatigue and enhancing safety
The system should limit the steering angle during high-speed lane changes on highways to prevent oversteering and loss of control
The acceleration control system must use predictive algorithms to smooth out acceleration and deceleration in heavy traffic, reducing the risk of rear-end collisions
The vehicle control system shall automatically decelerate when a lane change in heavy traffic is detected without safe distances
The vehicle's onboard systems must log steering and acceleration patterns during various traffic scenarios to inform future safety enhancements
